guide_text:
# Senior backend interview preparation

A twelve-week program for senior backend or backend-leaning platform and product roles. Work is ordered by transfer value: delivery and system-design foundations in Weeks 1–3; reusable architecture patterns and full-design application in Weeks 4–6; concrete backend technologies in Weeks 7–9; interview simulation and target-company calibration in Weeks 10–12.

Each week reserves twelve focused hours across system design, coding-mechanism understanding, behavioral preparation, plan-local closed-book retrieval, and optional desk implementation. Global Unprompted card reviews continue separately in Today and never determine Study Plan progress. Coding-pattern recognition, invariants, state transitions, complexity, and failure modes are core; writing code is optional and desk-only. Full system designs happen outside the conversational review flow. Every external practice session ends with a gap harvest, and readiness is based on observed external performance rather than card scores.

phases.description: Build the delivery method and core mechanisms that every later design uses.
Apply reusable scaling, resilience, workflow, and realtime patterns in full designs.
Map concrete data, messaging, search, and coordination systems onto the reusable mechanisms.
Convert knowledge into repeatable performance through mocks and focused gap repair.

items.title: Complete the system design delivery framework lesson
Turn functional and non-functional requirements into design constraints
Understand two-pointer, sliding-window, and interval recognition cues, invariants, complexity, and failure modes
Optional desk implementation: solve one representative problem from each Week 1 coding family
Deliver one requirements-to-deep-dives system design
Review the design and harvest specific mechanism gaps
Reconstruct the delivery framework closed-book

weeks.full_title: Request paths, network failures, identity, and data access

items.title: Trace request paths and network failure handling
Study API mechanics, authentication, and authorization boundaries
Understand stack, linked-list, and binary-search recognition cues, invariants, complexity, and failure modes
Optional desk implementation: solve one representative problem from each Week 2 coding family
Model entities and access patterns for one backend design
Review failure paths and harvest mechanism gaps
Reconstruct the request path and trust boundaries closed-book
Study caching, invalidation, and cache failure modes
Study sharding, consistent hashing, replication, and CAP
Understand heap, depth-first-search, and breadth-first-search recognition cues, invariants, complexity, and failure modes
Optional desk implementation: solve one representative problem from each Week 3 coding family
Design a partitioned and replicated storage path
Review consistency decisions and harvest mechanism gaps
Reconstruct partitioning and consistency trade-offs closed-book

weeks.full_title: Scaling reads, writes, replicas, and fan-out

items.title: Study read scaling, write scaling, replica lag, fan-out, backpressure, and queues
Complete a read-heavy full system design
Complete a write-heavy full system design
Understand graph, topological-ordering, and shortest-path recognition cues, invariants, complexity, and failure modes
Optional desk implementation: solve graph, dependency-ordering, and shortest-path problems
Start the behavioral story catalog with scope and ownership
Harvest and reconstruct scaling gaps
Study contention, distributed locks, and overload containment
Study sagas, durable workflows, circuit breakers, and exactly-once effects
Complete a workflow-heavy full system design
Complete a failure-heavy full system design
Understand backtracking, dynamic-programming, and greedy invariants; add ambiguity and perseverance stories
Optional desk implementation: solve representative backtracking, dynamic-programming, and greedy problems
Harvest and reconstruct resilience gaps

weeks.full_title: Realtime delivery, large jobs, and reliable events

items.title: Study realtime updates, large blobs, and long-running jobs
Study transactional outboxes and recovery after interrupted delivery
Complete a realtime full system design
Complete a platform-control-plane full system design
Understand trie, prefix-sum, and matrix-traversal invariants; complete the behavioral story catalog
Optional desk implementation: solve representative trie, prefix-sum, and matrix problems
Harvest and reconstruct platform mechanism gaps

weeks.full_title: Relational, cache, and wide-column data systems

items.title: Study PostgreSQL and Redis mechanics and failure modes
Study DynamoDB and Cassandra data modeling trade-offs
Reconstruct coding-pattern choices, invariants, complexity, and edge cases from representative prompts
Optional desk implementation: complete two timed coding sessions
Choose and defend storage technologies in one full design
Practice the Big Three behavioral answers
Reconstruct database selection trade-offs closed-book

weeks.full_title: Messaging, search, gateways, and content delivery

items.title: Study Kafka, API gateway, and asynchronous delivery mechanics
Study Elasticsearch, blob storage, CDN, rate limiting, and time-series behavior
Compare coding-pattern solution strategies and explain their invariants, complexity, and failure modes
Optional desk implementation: complete two timed coding sessions
Design a searchable media or document delivery system
Practice the Big Three behavioral answers with follow-ups
Reconstruct messaging and search trade-offs closed-book

weeks.full_title: Coordination, stream processing, and specialized indexes

items.title: Study Flink, ZooKeeper, and coordination guarantees
Study approximate structures, proximity search, and vector indexes
Decompose unfamiliar coding prompts into recognition cues, state, invariants, complexity, and edge cases
Optional desk implementation: complete two timed coding sessions
Design a streaming or proximity-search system
Practice senior-scope behavioral follow-ups
Reconstruct coordination and index trade-offs closed-book

weeks.full_title: Baseline interview simulations and gap diagnosis

items.title: Complete two full system design mocks
Walk through three coding prompts verbally: choose the pattern, maintain its invariant, analyze complexity, and test edge cases
Optional desk implementation: complete one timed coding mock
Complete two behavioral practices with follow-ups
Compare mock performance with the senior readiness gates
Repair the highest-impact observed gap
Reconstruct the repaired mechanism closed-book
Complete two target-shaped system design mocks
Walk through three target-shaped coding prompts verbally, including complexity and manual edge-case testing
Optional desk implementation: complete one plain-editor coding mock
Complete two behavioral practices with senior-scope follow-ups
Review evidence for the active target-company loop
Repair the highest-impact observed gap
Reconstruct the repaired mechanism closed-book
Complete two final full system design mocks
Walk through three final coding prompts verbally and explain pattern choice, invariants, complexity, and edge cases
Optional desk implementation: complete one final timed coding mock
Complete two final behavioral practices
Evaluate external performance against every readiness gate
Write the remaining-gap plan for scheduled interviews
Reconstruct the final repaired mechanism closed-book
